 JUDGMENT

The Petitioner filed this petition under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989 for claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-.
2.

The case of the Petitioner as follows:
According to the Petitioner that on 04-05- 2022 at about 7-30 p.m. when her son i.e.,
d e c e a s e d S r i . K h u s h a l R a j . R . w a s r i d i n g a m o t o r c y c l e b e a r i n g Reg.No.KA-53/HK-4785 proceeding on Jayanthi Grama road, Horamavu Bengaluru,
when he reached near Chamundeshwari temple, at that time, driver of one Tractor bearing No.KA-16/ TB-8794 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, came at high speed so as to endangering human life and dashed to the deceased motor cycle.
As a result the deceased fell down and died on the spot.

Immediately after the accident deadbody was shifted to East Point Hospital for 3 SCCH - 19 MVC. 2837 / 2022 post mortem and after post mortem, deadbody was handed over to the Petitioner and she shifted the same to her native place and performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased, for which she spent morethan Rs.2,00,000/- towards funeral expenses and other expenses.
It is further stated that, at the time of accident, the deceased was healthy and was a Student studying in 2nd year B.Com at Presidency College, Bangalore,
It is further stated that,
due to the sudden death of deceased, she lost love and affection of the deceased and undergoing great mental shock and mental agony.

3. It is further stated that, the accident in question occurred purely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor bearing No.KA-16/TB-8794, against whom the K.R.Puram Traffic police have registered a case in Crime No.73/2022 Punishable under section 279, 304(A) of IPC.
Hence, prayed to grant compensation.
4. In pursuance to the notice, Respondent No.1 and 2 did not appear before the Tribunal, hence they were placed exparte.

On the basis of the pleadings the Points that arise for my consideration are as under:
POINTS 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, on 04-05-2022 at about 7-30 p.m. her son i.e.,
deceased Sri.Khushal Raj .R. was riding a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53/
HK-4785 proceeding on Jayanthi Grama road, Horamavu Bengaluru, when he reached near Chamundeshwari temple, at that time, driver of one Tractor bearing Smt. Jayanthi .K vs Smt. Hanumakka on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34475935/
2 No.KA-16/TB-8794 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, came at high speed so as to endangering human life and dashed to the deceased motor cycle.
As a result the deceased fell down and died on the spot?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3.
Whether order or award?

6. In order to prove the case, Petitioner got examined as PW.1 and produced in all 17 documents marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P17.
7.
Heard the arguments of learned Counsel for the Petitioner and Perused the materials available on hand.

For the following reasons, I answer to the above Points as under:-
Point No.1: In the Affirmative, Point No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Point No.3: As per final order for the following:
REASONS 9. Point No.1:-

it is specific case of the Petitioner that, on 04-05-2022 at about 7-30 p.m. son of the Petitioner i.e., deceased Sri.Khushal Raj .R. was riding a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 53/HK-4785 proceeding on Jayanthi Grama road, Horamavu Bengaluru, when he reached near Chamundeshwari temple, at that time, driver of one Tractor bearing No.KA-16/TB-8794 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, came at high speed and dashed to the deceased motor cycle.
As a result the deceased fell down and died on the spot.
10. The Petitioner Smt.Jayanthi got examined herself as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination.
In her chief affidavit, she had reiterated the entire contention of petition and got 6 SCCH - 19 MVC. 2837 / 2022 marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P17 documents.
Ex.P1 is the Copy of F.I.R. Ex.P2 is the Copy of Complaint, Ex.P3 is the Copy of Spot Mahazar, Ex.P4 is the Copy of Spot Sketch,

Ex.P5 is the Copy of IMV report, Ex.P6 is the Copy of Inquest report, Ex.P7 is the Copy of PM report,
Ex.P8 is the Copy of Charge sheet, Ex.P9 is the copy of Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P10 is the copy of reply to the notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P11 is the Copy of Accused statement, Ex.P12 is the notarized copy of SSLC Marks card, Ex.P13 is the notarized copy of PUC Marks card, Ex.P14 & 15 are the Notarized Copy of the Aadhaar cards, Ex,P16 is the notarized copy of College ID Card and Ex.P17 is the notarized copy of college fee receipt.
11. On perusal of Ex.P4 - Spot sketch it discloses that accident occurred on Jayanthi Grama road,
Horamavu Bengaluru, in front of Hindustan bedding centre shop, driver of Tractor bearing Smt. Jayanthi .K vs Smt. Hanumakka on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34475935/
3 No.KA-16/TB-8794 drove the same initially on middle of the road and then took his vehicle to left turn and dashed the deceased motor cycle and caused the accident.

Further on perusal of Ex.P11 statement given by the accused / driver of the offending vehicle before Police Inspector, K.R.Traffic P.S. admitting the accident caused by him to the deceased near BBMP junction Horamavu, Bengaluru and after the accident he had shifted the injured to the Dr.B.R.Ambedkar Hospital.
Further the driver stated that the offending vehicle is in the name of his mother and no insurance to the vehicle and not registered the Tanker.

The K.R.Puram Traffic police filed the Charge sheet against Tractor bearing No.KA-16/TB-8794.
13.

In the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the claimant has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble APEX Court inthe decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.text: 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The so-called reason that as the name of Dheeraj Kumar was not mentioned in the FIR, so it was not possible for Dheeraj Kumar to see the incident, is not a proper assessment of the fact- situation in this case.
It is well known that in a case relating to motor accident claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as it is required to be 8 SCCH - 19 MVC. 2837 / 2022 done in a criminal trial.
The Court must keep this distinction in mind.

10. Reference in this connection may be made to the decision of this Court in Bimla Devi and others V/ s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, in which the relevant observation on this point has been made and which is very pertinent and is quoted below:-

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others V/ s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touch stone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."

14. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P1 - F.I.R. Ex.P2 - Complaint, Ex.P3 - Spot Mahazar, Ex.P4 - Spot Sketch, Ex.P5 - IMV report, Ex.P6 - Inquest report, Ex.P7 - PM report, Ex.P8 - Charge sheet, Ex.P9 - Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P10 - reply to the notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act & Ex.P11 is the Copy of Accused statement it appears that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Therefore considering all these aspects I come to conclusion that, the said accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the 9 SCCH - 19 MVC.
2837 / 2022 Tractor bearing No.KA-16/TB-8794.
Accordingly I answer Point no.1 in the affirmative.
15. Point No.2:-
The Petitioner claims compensation amount of Rs.50,00,000/- with respect to death of her son Mr.Kushal Raj .R. in a road traffic accident.

The Petitioner stated that, due to Smt. Jayanthi .K vs Smt. Hanumakka on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34475935/
4 sudden death of the deceased she lost love, affection and future support of the deceased and also she undergoing great mental agony and hardship.
16.
To prove the age of the deceased, the Petitioner produced Notarized copy of SSLC Marks card which is marked as Ex.P12.
As per said document, date of birth of the deceased is shown as 06-11-2001.
This accident occurred in the year 2022.
Hence the age of the deceased is taken into consideration as 21 years at the time of accident.

Then the proper multiplier is 18.
17.
The Petitioner stated that, prior to the date of accident the deceased was healthy and studying in 2nd year B.Com., at Presidency College.

The Petitioner had produced College ID card of the 10 SCCH - 19 MVC. 2837 / 2022 deceased at Ex.P16 and fee receipt issued by said Presidency college,
which discloses that the deceased Mr.Kushal Raj .R. was a 2 nd year B.com., student.

The counsel for the Petitioner relied upon following Judgments & citations:
1. MFA.No.103473/2017 (MV) passed by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Dharwad Bench, in the case of Sri.Basavaraj V/s Sri.Uesh and another.,
2. MFA.No.8727/2018 (MV) passed by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru in the case of Kum.Anusha V/s H.S.Surendra and another.,
3. 2017 ACJ 2153, Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in the case of Oriental Ins., Co.
ltd., V/s Roopa Bai and another.
In the above said case laws

sentences.text: the loss of future income is considered based on notional income in the case of Student aged about 14 years.
So, same is applicable to present case also.
The deceased was a student studying in 2 nd year B.com and the Petitioner has also produced college fee receipt.
In a present days the Coolie worker gets Rs.400/- to 500/- per day.
Therefore, by considering the age and Qualification of the deceased, this Tribunal taken notional income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/- p.m. 11 SCCH - 19 MVC. 2837 / 2022 18.

With regard to the loss of future prospectus is concern, the Apex court in the earlier Judgment reported in 2013 ACJ 1403 (Rajesh & Ors Vs Rajbir Singh & Ors) also taken note of the fact that, self employed persons are also entitled for future prospectus and the said Judgment was referred to larger bench and the Apex court in the recent Judgment passed in 2017 ACJ 2700 SC (between National Insurance co. ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others.)

entities.text: 2013 ACJ 1403 (Rajesh & Ors Vs Rajbir Singh & Ors)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance co. ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "In case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.

An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component"
Herein this case, the deceased aged about 21 years at the time of accident.
Hence the Petitioner is entitled to claim 40% of future prospectus as per above citation, due to death of the deceased in the road traffic accident.

5 19.
It is pertinent to note that, the Petitioner is the mother of the deceased.
Hence the Petitioner is 12 SCCH - 19 MVC. 2837 / 2022 considered as dependent on the income of the deceased.

So relying upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarla Varma and others -Vs- Delhi Transport Corporation & another), out of the salary of the deceased 50% has to be deducted towards Personal expenses of the deceased as the deceased is the Unmarried / Bachelor.

sentences.text:
a) Income of deceased is taken at Rs. 15,000-00 b) Addition of 40% income towards future prospectus @ Rs.15,000/- + Rs. 21,000-00 Rs.6,000/-
(40%)
c) Deduction towards personal expenses:
 Rs. 10,500-00  Out of Rs.21000/- - (50%) =
 Rs.10,500/-
Therefore this tribunal taken monthly income of the deceased at Rs.10,500/-, which comes as under:-
Rs.10,500 X 12 X 18 = Rs.22,68,000/- Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.22,68,000/- under the head loss of dependency.
20. The Petitioner is the mother of the deceased, she lost love, affection and future support of the deceased.

In this regard the Hon'ble Supreme 13 SCCH - 19 MVC. 2837 / 2022 Court of India was held in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram & Ors., (Civil Appeal No.9581/2018 (Arising out of SLP (civil) 3192/2018)

entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram & Ors.,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation aimed at providing relief to the victims or their families, in cases of genuine claims.
In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of Filial Consortium.
Parental consortium is awarded to children who lose their parents in motor vehicle accidents under the Act.
A few High courts have awarded compensation on this count.
However, there was no clarity with respect to the principles on which compensation could be awarded on loss of Filial Consortium.

The amount of compensation to be awarded as consortium will be governed by the Principles of awarding compensation under "Loss of consortium"
Smt. Jayanthi .K vs Smt. Hanumakka on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34475935/
6 as laid down in Pranay Sethi (Supra).
In the present case, we deem it appropriate to award the father and the sister of the deceased, an amount of Rs.40,000/- each, for loss of Filial Consortium.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled compensation for an amount of Rs.40,000/- under the head loss of Filial Consortium.
14 SCCH - 19 MVC. 2837 / 2022 21.

The Petitioner claimed that, she had spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body,
funeral and obsequies ceremonies of the deceased.
but she has not produced any document in this respect.

Considering the expenses towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies of the deceased and in view of judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court passed in 2017 ACJ 2700 SC (between National Insurance co. ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others), it is just and proper to award a Rs.15,000/- under this head.

entities.text: National Insurance co. ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Petitioners are also entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head loss of estate.

22. Considering oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:
Sl.
 Under the Heads of Amount No.
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 22,68,000-00 2.
Towards Filial Consortium Rs. 40,000-00 3. Towards funeral and Rs. 15,000-00  obsequies ceremonies 4.
Towards loss of estate Rs. 15,000-00  Total Rs. 23,38,000-00  15 SCCH - 19  MVC. 2837 / 2022  The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.23,38,000/-.
23. Interest:

In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held Smt. Jayanthi .K vs Smt. Hanumakka on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34475935/
7 that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim Petitions has to be 6% p.a.
and not more than that.

entities.text: Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6%
p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
24. Liability:-
As per the petition Respondent No.1 is the Owner and Respondent No.2 is the driver of the Tractor bearing No.KA-16/TB-8794.
As already discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

It is 16 SCCH - 19 MVC. 2837 / 2022 pertinent to note that after service of summons the Respondents did not appear before the Tribunal and contest the case of the Petitioner, hence the respondents No.1 and 2 were placed exparte.
Therefore adverse inference to be drawn against the Respondents.
The oral and documentary evidence of the Petitioner is unrebutted & unchallenged.
Accordingly, Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Further, the Respondent No.1 being Owner of the offending vehicle is primarily held liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.2 in the Partly Affirmative.

25. Point No.3: for the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder.
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.23,38,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 & 2 jointly and severally liable to pay aforesaid compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Further, the Respondent No.1 being Owner of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within Sixty days, from the date of this Order.

After deposit, out of total compensation amount a sum of Rs.15,38,000/- with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner with proper identification and the remaining amount with interest shall be deposited in her name in FD in any nationalized bank, for a period of Three years,
with a liberty to withdraw the accrued interest periodically.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

25. Point No.3: for the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder.
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.23,38,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
17 SCCH - 19 MVC. 2837 / 2022
The Respondent No.1 & 2 jointly and severally liable to pay aforesaid compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Further, the Respondent No.1 being Owner of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within Sixty days, from the date of this Order.
After deposit, out of total compensation amount a sum of Rs.15,38,000/- with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner with proper identification and the remaining amount with interest shall be deposited in her name in FD in any nationalized bank, for a period of Three years,
with a liberty to withdraw the accrued interest periodically.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
